text:
maya: Quick design check — I'm iterating on the model catalog filter rail and the small legend that explains performance badges. Want to align on 1) filter hierarchy labeling, 2) how pinning a version affects compare rows, and 3) a11y + keyboard affordances. Posting a screenshot + proposed copy below.

ben: thanks! can you paste the screenshot link?

maya: https://img.redwood-ui/mockups/model-catalog-legend-v3.png — top-left shows 'Performance' badge legend (fast/cost/quality) and the filter rail has 'Model attributes' > 'Performance' > checkboxes.

arjun: high-level thought: users glance at the legend for quick triage. make the badge semantics scannable in 1 line each. avoid long sentences.

maya: agreed. current microcopy: 
```
Performance badges explain expected latency/cost/quality tradeoffs.
Fast — for low-latency, higher cost.
Efficient — balanced latency and cost.
High Quality — best for accuracy-sensitive tasks.
```

sam: nit: "Fast — for low-latency, higher cost." -> "Fast — low latency, higher cost." shorter. same for others.

tia: also consider using icons + accessible names for screen readers (aria-labels). e.g., aria-label="Performance: Fast".

ben: on pinning: what happens when you pin a version in the compare table? do we lock that column from other upgrades and prevent automatic fallback?

maya: idea: pinning should be local to the user's compare session (not global), and pinned columns should be visually persistent and excluded from auto-sort when a new model version enters results. Should we show a small 'Pinned' chip and a keyboard shortcut to toggle?

arjun: sounds right. UX question: if a pinned version goes offline or becomes incompatible, show a warning row-level and do not silently swap. explicit fallback button only.

sam: accessibility note: pinned column needs clear focus ring and should be reachable via TAB. also add an aria-describedby to explain pinned behavior.

maya: proposed microcopy for the pinned tooltip: 
```
Pinned — this version is held for side-by-side comparison. It won't be auto-swapped by rollouts or filters. Click to unpin.
```

ben: suggestion: change "held for side-by-side comparison" -> "held for comparison" (shorter). Also replace "Click" with "Select" because keyboard users won't click. => "Select to unpin."

tia: +1. final tooltip: 
```
Pinned — this version is held for comparison. It won't be auto-swapped by rollouts or filters. Select to unpin.
```

maya: cool. now the filter hierarchy: I had two options — group filters by "Model" vs "Behavior" or by "Attributes" vs "Performance". Which maps better to user mental models?

arjun: customers ask for "Performance" as first-class (latency/cost/quality) so keep that top-level. "Attributes" can be a second group for model size, architecture.

sam: small tweak: show counts next to filters (e.g., Performance (12)) — but ensure these counts are accessible (aria-live updates when filters applied).

ben: UX for keyboard: filter chip should be focusable, Space/Enter toggles, and Home/End to jump groups. document shortcuts in the help overlay (/?).

maya: noted. one more thing — the legend contrast: current green/blue/amber palette fails contrast at small sizes. tia any quick color suggestions that pass AA?

tia: recommend desaturating the amber slightly and increasing weight for icons. I'll drop 2 hex options in the Figma file by EOD. Also add a 2px stroke for small badge icons to help on low-DPI screens.

maya: perfect. next steps: Tia will update colors + accessibility tokens, Ben will wordsmith pinned tooltip and filter copy, Arjun will spec fallback UX for pinned offline, Sam will draft keyboard interactions, and I'll push a small PR with the updated legend and the pinned chip visuals.

ben: timeline?

maya: aiming for a lightweight PR by Thu (three days). if blockers, call it out here.

ui-bot: Reminder: design review sync scheduled Thu 10:30am PT in #design-review.

sam: noted, I'll prototype keyboard flows tomorrow.

arjun: will draft the fallback mock in the afternoon.

tia: updating Figma now.

maya: thanks everyone :heart:
